items.summary: The Bengaluru Urban district election office has admitted that some voters in the Byatarayanapura Assembly constituency were wrongly marked as having “No mapping” despite having correct records in the 2002 electoral roll. The office, however, said these voters will still have to undergo an inquiry by election officials. According to a press note issued on Wednesday, September 2, the Election Registration Officer (ERO) and Assistant Electoral Registration Officer (AERO) will examine such cases, collect documents from the concerned voters and verify their eligibility. The Additional District Election Officer (ADEO) will subsequently ensure that eligible voters are included in the final electoral roll. The admission came after reports alleged irregularities in the digitisation and mapping of voter samples during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the 152-Byatarayanapura constituency. The district election office said it scrutinised several polling booths in the constituency, including booths 158, 284, 206, 161, 163, 167, 168, 176 and 177. items.title: RSS not a political party: Karnataka tribunal stays teacher's suspension for attending RSS event
items.summary: The Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal (KSAT) at Kalburgi has stayed the suspension of a government school teacher who participated in a Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) event [Gururaj v. State of Karnataka]. A coram of Judicial Member SY Watawati and Administrative Member Dr Amita Prasad said that the school teacher had not violated the Karnataka State Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 2021 that prevents government servants from attending functions organised by political parties or by associations that participate in politics. The Tribunal further held the applicant had not violated any State government order or notification that explicitly barred participation in events. It further held the RSS to be a non-political party. "When he participated in the event organized by a non-political party, the act of the applicant did not violate the conditions stipulated under Rule 5 of the Conduct Rules, 2021 referred to supra. Further, the State Government has not issued any order or notification prohibiting any Government Official from participating in such an event." items.title: HarperCollins steps in to publish Sonia Gandhi memoir Belonging after Penguin fallout
items.summary: Congress leader Sonia Gandhi’s upcoming memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love , has found a new publisher in HarperCollins India after a sudden fallout with Penguin Random House India over editorial differences. HarperCollins announced on Friday, September 4, that it will publish the book on November 10, 2026. The development comes days after Penguin Random House India (PRHI) pulled back from releasing the title, citing an impasse over "a particular issue" during the editing process. The book was originally announced in mid-August by US publisher Alfred A. Knopf as a global release, with PRHI handling the Indian edition and planning a print run of 100,000 copies. However, negotiations stalled during editorial review. News reports, citing sources, indicated that differences arose over political commentary in the manuscript, including Sonia Gandhi’s observations about Prime Minister Narendra Modi during official meetings, her thoughts on being called certain derogatory names by Modi during campaigning, her perspective on India-China relations, and her views on the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS). items.title: NLSIU, TNNLU, GNLU still not on BCI's approved list of law colleges; deadline extended for fifth time
items.summary: The Bar Council of India (BCI), for the fifth time, has extended the deadline for existing Centres of Legal Education (CLEs) to submit applications for extension of approval for the 2026-27 academic session. The new cut-off date is September 15. It was originally fixed at December 31, 2025, before being pushed to January 16, then March 5, then July 31 and most recently to August 31. As of the fourth deadline extension , 4 National Law Universities (NLUs) remained without BCI approval: National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru; National Law Institute University (NLIU), Bhopal; Tamil Nadu National Law University (TNNLU), Tiruchirappalli and Gujarat National Law University (GNLU), Gandhinagar. NLIU has since secured renewal, while NLSIU, TNNLU and GNLU continue to remain without BCI approval. The notice states that the extension applies only to existing CLEs seeking extension of approval for existing courses at previously sanctioned intake for the 2026-27 academic session. All concerned CLEs have been asked to complete pending requirements, including uploading their respective university's affiliation order for 2026-27 and the requisite fee, within the extended period

Singh's practice focuses on international commercial and investment treaty arbitration, complex cross-border litigation, and white-collar investigations. Qualified to practice in India, New York, and England and Wales, Aditya worked in White & Case’s New York and London offices before moving to Singapore. He also sits as arbitrator and is an Adjunct Associate Professor at the National University of Singapore (NUS) Faculty of Law. A graduate of NALSAR and the Yale Law School, Singh has acted in some of the largest and most closely watched international disputes involving Indian parties. Earlier this year, Singh was part of the team that successfully represented India before the High Court of Australia in enforcement proceedings arising from Devas v Republic of India BIT award . Most recently, Singh represented a defendant in United States v Adani et al , the closely watched US proceedings concerning allegations of conspiracy to violate the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act. items.title: Service case stemming from ₹67: Delhi HC slaps ₹1 lakh costs on DTC for 32-year-old litigation against conductor
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has imposed costs of ₹1 lakh on Delhi Transport Corporation (DTC) for pursuing a case for 32 years against a conductor's claim for 17 months' back wages [ DTC vs Rajender Prashad ]. The case itself stemmed from the conductor's dismissal for allegedly taking ₹67 from passengers without issuing tickets to them. In the judgment delivered on September 2, Justice Amit Mahajan observed that the prolonged dispute resulted in abuse of the process of law and avoidable expenditure of public money. Hence, it refused to entertain the petition filed by DTC challenging a 2004 award passed by the Industrial Tribunal, which had allowed the conductor’s claim for back wages. “The continued litigation over such a limited claim, for an inordinately long period, amounts to an abuse of the process of law and has resulted in avoidable expenditure of public money,” the Court stated. Justice Amit Mahajan, Delhi High Court The industrial dispute dating back to 1994, pertained to DTC’s action against its bus conductor, Rajender Prashad, for allegedly taking ₹67 from the passengers without issuing tickets to them. items.title: 2026 ICC Arbitration Rules: Navigating the era of efficiency and procedural innovation
items.summary: The International Chamber of Commerce have recently released the ICC Arbitration Rules, 2026 wherein substantial changes have been introduced by the International Chamber of Commerce reflecting the move to enhance transparency, efficiency, user friendliness and expediting the international arbitration practice. The newly introduced rules have entered into force on June 1, 2026 and will be applicable to the arbitrations commencing from June 1, 2026 unless otherwise agreed by the parties to be governed by the previous rules of the year 2021. Key takeaways and analysis of the changes Highly expedited arbitration procedures An altogether new procedural model has been introduced by the revised rules for expeditious resolution, which, unlike the expedited procedure, does not apply on the basis of the monetary threshold but is entirely consensual in nature. The parties to the arbitration in accordance with Article 33 read with Appendix VI can agree to the resolution of the dispute through the Highly Expedited Arbitration Procedure under the aegis of the ICC Revised Rules, 2026 . items.title: Supreme Court’s recent arbitration rulings have created grave uncertainty: Retired Justice Rohinton Nariman
items.summary: Former Supreme Court Justice Rohinton F Nariman recently said that some of the Supreme Court’s recent arbitration judgments were incorrect and had created “grave uncertainty” by reopening settled questions. Justice Nariman was delivering the keynote address at the Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre’s Arbitration Week 2026. He examined 5 recent Constitution Bench decisions concerning the appointment of arbitrators and challenges to arbitral awards. “ Here we have five recent judgments of the Supreme Court. How has the Act fared? According to me, not particularly well, because, firstly, the judgments don’t conduce to certainty . Secondly, constantly reopening closed questions again leads to grave uncertainty. Some of the judgments, unfortunately, are on the face of them not correct, in my humble submission .” Justice Nariman first referred to the five-judge ruling in Cox and Kings . The judgment held that the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 had to be read with the Contract Act while deciding whether a non-signatory intended to be bound by an arbitration agreement.
